_comment: Models the Welder ML worker can download. Welder reads this file too (to show what a node needs). Files go to <ml home>/models/<id>/; a finished download writes <id>/.complete.

ltx-2.5.label: LTX-2.5 22B (distilled transformer, Gemma text encoder, VAEs, upscaler)
ltx-2.5.license: LTX-2 Community License (free under $10M annual revenue)

ltx-ic-upscaler.label: LTX-2.5 IC-LoRA: Pixel Spatial Upscaler x2

ltx-ic-union.label: LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA: Union Control (depth / pose / edges)

ltx-ic-sdr-to-hdr.label: LTX-2.5 IC-LoRA: SDR to HDR (with its scene embeddings)

ltx-2.5-video-vae.label: LTX-2.5 video VAE (the one SDR to HDR decodes with)
ltx-2.5-video-vae.license: LTX-2 Community License (free under $10M annual revenue)

mapanything.label: MapAnything (Apache 2.0 weights): cameras + depth from frames

video-depth-anything-small.label: Video Depth Anything Small (relative depth, steady over time)

video-depth-anything-base.label: Video Depth Anything Base (relative depth, steady over time)

video-depth-anything-large.label: Video Depth Anything Large (relative depth, steady over time)

metric-video-depth-anything-small.label: Metric Video Depth Anything Small (metres, steady over time)

metric-video-depth-anything-base.label: Metric Video Depth Anything Base (metres, steady over time)

metric-video-depth-anything-large.label: Metric Video Depth Anything Large (metres, steady over time)

sam2.1-hiera-tiny.label: SAM 2.1 Hiera Tiny (TrackMask: click an object, it's masked through the shot)

sam2.1-hiera-small.label: SAM 2.1 Hiera Small (TrackMask: click an object, it's masked through the shot)

sam2.1-hiera-base-plus.label: SAM 2.1 Hiera Base Plus (TrackMask: click an object, it's masked through the shot)

owlv2-base.label: OWLv2 base (TrackMask: find objects from text)

corridorkey-2.label: CorridorKey 2.0 (Corridor Digital) with C-RADIOv4, MoGe-2 and RVM
corridorkey-2.license: Corridor Key Licence 2.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 + additional terms): free to use on commercial projects, your output is yours; no reselling or paid inference. Foundation models: NVIDIA Open Model License (C-RADIOv4), MIT (MoGe-2), CC-BY 4.0 (RVM)
corridorkey-2.install_note:
CorridorKey isn't a single Hugging Face download. By hand: download https://github.com/nikopueringer/CorridorKey2.0/archive/485f5e9ab759ead6138cc990776184b59d6ea971.zip, unzip it so this folder holds its corridorkey/, scripts/ and third_party/ folders, then run (with the ML environment's python):
  python scripts/download_weights.py --package_root "<this folder>"
It fetches the CorridorKey weights and the C-RADIOv4, MoGe-2 and RVM foundation models (about 5 GB) into weights/ and vfms/. The layout matters: keep its folders.

ic_loras._comment: Presets for the LTX node. model: the models entry; control: what the reference video is made of (input = the src input as is). prompt: the template the panel's 'template' button puts in the prompt; replace the <...> parts. stages: the default recipe ('one', 'two', 'two + IC-LoRA'). style: 'wanted' warns when the style input is empty. src_label: what the src input is called on this preset. canny: [low, high] defaults. max_size / chunk_frames: the preset's defaults for those knobs; min_frames: windows are at least this long. pipeline 'hdr': Lightricks' SDR-to-HDR pipeline instead of the IC-LoRA one.

Layout to Render.prompt: <one or two sentences describing the finished shot, matching the style frame>
Layout to Render.note: layout: a clay render, playblast or blocky previs (camera, motion, placement). style: a finished-looking first frame (make one with ImageGen), not a grey clay frame. Don't write 'clay', '3D' or 'Unreal' in the prompt. 24 fps; 1920x1088 is a known good size.

Clean Plate.prompt: <describe the empty scene>. No <what to remove>.
Clean Plate.note: Removes people or objects from the shot. Describe the scene as it looks empty and name what to remove. Validated up to 1920x1088.

Outpaint.note: Put src on the bigger canvas first (Reformat / Crop with transparent padding): what has no alpha is the new area. Or connect a mask (alpha = new area). Describe only what goes there.

Ingredients.prompt: Reference sheet: <one line per panel: the character, the prop, the location>. Generated video: <the action>
Ingredients.note: src: a reference sheet (one image: a clean panel per character / prop and one for the location, on black); a still is fine. The frame range sets the length (121 frames or more). Its aspect sets the output's; trained at 768x448.

Instant Shave.prompt: REMOVEBEARD <describe the person and the scene>
Instant Shave.note: LTX-2.3 adapter. Removes beards; keep REMOVEBEARD at the start of the prompt.

Pixel Upscaler x4.note: LTX-2.3 adapter. Output is four times the input size; best from a small draft (around 280p). It invents detail.

SDR to HDR.note: Lightricks' HDR pipeline: the whole range in one pass, no prompt. The result is scene-linear HDR (values above 1). src should be an SDR plate (sRGB).

Alpha Gen.note: Returns a matte (white = foreground). Prompt stays empty.

Pixel Upscaler x2.note: Output is twice the input size; it invents detail, it is not a pixel-accurate upscale.

Water Simulation.prompt: Reference shows <the scene>. Edited shows the same scene with water added. ADD WATER <describe the result>. The identity, layout and framing stay identical to the reference.
Water Simulation.note: Describe the water. Keep the ADD WATER trigger.

Colorization.prompt: Reference shows <the scene>. Edited shows the same scene with natural colors restored. COLORIZE <describe the result>. Only color information differs between reference and edited.
Colorization.note: Lower the strength to 0.8-0.9 if colours bleed.

Decompression.prompt: Reference shows <the scene>, heavily compressed with visible macroblocking. ENHANCE QUALITY <describe the result>. Only compression artifacts and image quality differ between reference and edited.

Deblur.prompt: Reference shows <the scene>, out of focus. Edited shows the same scene in sharp focus. DEBLUR <describe the result>
Deblur.note: For defocus, not motion blur. Sweep strength 0.5-1.

Day to Night.prompt: Reference shows <the scene> in daylight. Edited shows the same scene at night: <describe the result>. Only the lighting changes from day to night.

Union Control (depth).note: LTX-2.3 adapter on LTX-2.5 (as Lightricks' 2.5 workflows do). The depth video is made from src with Video Depth Anything Small (or feed a depth pass and choose control 'input'). Describe the look, not the motion.

Union Control (edges).note: LTX-2.3 adapter on LTX-2.5 (as Lightricks' 2.5 workflows do). Canny edges are made from src (Lightricks use thresholds 92 / 200). Describe the look, not the motion.

Union Control (as is).note: LTX-2.3 adapter on LTX-2.5 (as Lightricks' 2.5 workflows do). Feed a depth, pose or edge video into src yourself. Describe the look, not the motion.

Union Control (pose).note: LTX-2.3 adapter on LTX-2.5 (as Lightricks' 2.5 workflows do). Pose skeletons (body, hands, face) are made from src with DWPose. Describe the look, not the motion.

Motion Control.note: src: the shot with coloured motion-path splines drawn over it (e.g. RotoPaint strokes).

Inpaint.note: The mask input (alpha) marks what to replace; it is painted #66FF00 into the reference. Include shadows in the mask.

Relight.prompt: relight the video to match the light-direction ball. <describe the result>
Relight.note: A shaded ball showing the light direction is drawn top right of every frame. Describe the look and where the light comes from.
